questions.prompt: An NMOS has \(\mu_nC_{ox} = 300\ \mu\mathrm{A/V^2}\), \(W/L = 8\), \(V_{ov} = 0.6\ \mathrm{V}\) and \(V_{DS} = 0.2\ \mathrm{V}\). Using the triode equation, find \(I_D\) in µA.
questions.figure_alt: NMOS output characteristics: for each overdrive the current rises in triode, then flattens in saturation; the dashed parabola V_DS = V_ov marks the boundary.

questions.prompt: For very small \(V_{DS}\), the same device acts as a resistor. What is \(R_{on} = 1/(\mu_nC_{ox}\frac WLV_{ov})\) in Ω?
questions.figure_alt: NMOS output characteristics: for each overdrive the current rises in triode, then flattens in saturation; the dashed parabola V_DS = V_ov marks the boundary.

questions.prompt: Why does the triode \(I_D\)-\(V_{DS}\) curve bend downward as \(V_{DS}\) grows?
options: The channel charge thins toward the drain, because the gate-to-channel voltage there is only \(V_{GS} - V_{DS}\)
questions.explanation: Local inversion charge is \(C_{ox}(V_{GS} - V(x) - V_T)\); at the drain end it is smaller, so the average conductance falls (the \(-V_{DS}/2\) term).

questions.prompt: A switch transistor must have \(R_{on} = 100\ \Omega\) at \(V_{ov} = 1.0\ \mathrm{V}\) with \(\mu_nC_{ox} = 250\ \mu\mathrm{A/V^2}\). What \(W/L\) is needed?

questions.prompt: A MOSFET in deep triode is used as a voltage-controlled resistor. Increasing \(V_{GS}\) does what to \(R_{on}\)?
questions.explanation: More gate overdrive means more inversion charge per area: conductance \(\propto V_{ov}\).
questions.figure_alt: NMOS output characteristics: for each overdrive the current rises in triode, then flattens in saturation; the dashed parabola V_DS = V_ov marks the boundary.

questions.prompt: In the device of the first question (\(\mu_nC_{ox}W/L = 2.4\ \mathrm{mA/V^2}\), \(V_{ov} = 0.6\ \mathrm{V}\)), what is the triode current at \(V_{DS} = V_{ov}\) (in µA), the edge of saturation?
questions.explanation: \(I_D = 2.4\ \mathrm{mA/V^2}\,(0.6 - 0.3)(0.6) = 432\ \mu\mathrm{A}\), which equals \(\tfrac12(2.4\ \mathrm{mA/V^2})(0.6)^2\): the triode and saturation formulas meet at the boundary.
questions.figure_alt: NMOS output characteristics: for each overdrive the current rises in triode, then flattens in saturation; the dashed parabola V_DS = V_ov marks the boundary.

questions.prompt: How much does the triode current at \(V_{DS} = 0.2\ \mathrm{V}\) fall short of the purely linear estimate \(\mu_nC_{ox}\frac WLV_{ov}V_{DS}\), with \(V_{ov} = 0.8\ \mathrm{V}\)? Give the shortfall in percent.
questions.explanation: Ratio \((V_{ov} - V_{DS}/2)/V_{ov} = 0.7/0.8 = 0.875\), a 12.5% shortfall. The linear model holds only for \(V_{DS} \ll V_{ov}\).
questions.figure_alt: NMOS output characteristics: for each overdrive the current rises in triode, then flattens in saturation; the dashed parabola V_DS = V_ov marks the boundary.

questions.prompt: A transmission-gate switch passes a 1 V signal. Its NMOS has the gate at 1.8 V and \(V_T = 0.5\ \mathrm{V}\), with the source at the 1 V signal. Compared with passing 0 V, its on-resistance is:
options: Lower, since the signal adds to the gate
questions.explanation: \(V_{ov} = 1.8 - 1 - 0.5 = 0.3\ \mathrm{V}\) versus 1.3 V at 0 V input: about 4× the resistance. That is why the PMOS is added in parallel.

questions.prompt: Integrating the channel conductance along the channel gives the triode formula. Which local relation is integrated?
questions.explanation: Drift current = (local sheet charge) × mobility × field × width. Integrating \(dy\) from 0 to \(L\) and \(dV\) from 0 to \(V_{DS}\) gives \((V_{ov} - V_{DS}/2)V_{DS}\).
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 360 170" role="img" aria-label="MOSFET channel cross-section: the inversion layer is thick at the source and thins toward the drain as V_DS rises (triode)." fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" style="max-width:360px;width:100%;height:auto"><rect x="20" y="80" width="320" height="80" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.10"/><rect x="40" y="80" width="60" height="24"/><rect x="260" y="80" width="60" height="24"/><text x="70" y="96" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">n+ S</text><text x="290" y="96" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">n+ D</text><rect x="100" y="50" width="160" height="24"/><text x="180" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">gate</text><polygon points="100,81 260,81 260,84 100,88" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.15"/><text x="180" y="120" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">inversion layer thins toward drain</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: MOSFET channel cross-section: the inversion layer is thick at the source and thins toward the drain as V_DS rises (triode).

questions.prompt: Preview of the square law: what happens to the triode expression if you set \(V_{DS} = V_{ov}\)?
options: It becomes \(\tfrac12\mu_nC_{ox}\frac WLV_{ov}^2\), the saturation current
questions.explanation: \((V_{ov} - V_{ov}/2)V_{ov} = V_{ov}^2/2\). The square law is the peak of the triode parabola.
questions.figure_alt: NMOS output characteristics: for each overdrive the current rises in triode, then flattens in saturation; the dashed parabola V_DS = V_ov marks the boundary.

questions.prompt: Preview of the square law: the triode parabola \(I_D(V_{DS})\) has its maximum at what \(V_{DS}\) (in V) for \(V_{ov} = 0.7\ \mathrm{V}\)?
questions.explanation: \(dI_D/dV_{DS} = \mu_nC_{ox}\frac WL(V_{ov} - V_{DS}) = 0\) at \(V_{DS} = V_{ov}\). Beyond it the real device saturates instead of following the parabola down.
questions.figure_alt: NMOS output characteristics: for each overdrive the current rises in triode, then flattens in saturation; the dashed parabola V_DS = V_ov marks the boundary.

questions.prompt: Preview of saturation: physically, what happens at the drain end when \(V_{DS} = V_{ov}\)?
options: The inversion layer pinches off: the gate-to-drain voltage just equals \(V_T\)
questions.explanation: \(V_{GD} = V_{GS} - V_{DS} = V_T\): the drain end is exactly at threshold.
